findings.issue_text: Scaffold: `docs/metareview/reviews/mrv-20260824-032556091354000-task-done-task-001-089a7fbe.md` — verdict **NEEDS_REVISION**, advisory gate effect.

`[deterministic/test-reviewer]` **mrvf-...-001 [high, blocking]** Missing test changes or validation evidence — source changed in `lib/post_creator.rb`, `lib/post_revisor.rb`, `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, `lib/topic_retriever.rb` without corresponding tests. (Partially a false positive: 4 new spec files were added — but none cover these four `lib/` files, so the substance holds.)
`[deterministic/manifest]` Manifest blocker: missing shard result for `shard-01` (all 29 files in one shard); runtime not assessed, static-only.

`[lens/feasibility+completeness+intent+architecture]` `app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6` — `<%- end if %>` is a Ruby syntax error. I independently confirmed by compiling the ERB: `syntax error, unexpected ';'` at `end if`. The primary success path (topic found) raises on every render. Should be `<%- end %>`.

`[lens/feasibility]` `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:43` — spec asserts `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)` + `retriever.expects(:retrieve)`, but `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15` calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and never touches `TopicRetriever`. Confirmed by grep; the mocha expectation is unsatisfiable.

`[lens/feasibility]` `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:50` — `TopicView.expects(:new).with(...)` has no `.returns`, so `@topic_view` is nil and the view raises `NoMethodError`, while the `after` block asserts `response.should be_success`.

`[lens/completeness+intent]` `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:1` — no `render_views` anywhere in the 4 new specs (confirmed by grep), which is precisely why the template syntax error above passes CI. No view/integration coverage of the feature's main output.

`[lens/feasibility+architecture]` `app/models/topic_embed.rb:48` — `open(url).read` with no `require 'open-uri'` in the file. Only `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:7` requires it; `import_remote` is reached from `lib/topic_retriever.rb:52` and `lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148` on paths that never load poll_feed, where `Kernel#open` treats the URL as a filename → `Errno::ENOENT`.

`[lens/scope+feasibility+architecture+intent]` `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3` — already-committed, unrelated migration edited to add `force: true`. Editing shipped migrations is unsafe; `force: true` issues `DROP TABLE` on any environment not yet past this version. Nothing in the embed feature touches `top_topics`.

`[lens/feasibility+architecture+completeness]` `db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3` — `force: true` on a new table silently drops/recreates rather than failing loudly; not the convention elsewhere in the repo.

`[lens/completeness+architecture]` `db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:4` — no indexes on `topic_id`/`post_id` despite both being queried/joined; no FKs; `embed_url` is a plain 255-char `:string` under a unique index, truncating longer canonical URLs.

`[lens/architecture]` `db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3` — `default: 1` hardcodes the numeric value of `Post.cook_methods[:regular]`; reordering the enum in `app/models/post.rb:63` silently desyncs the column default.

`[lens/intent+architecture]` `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:19` — `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring test, not origin equality. `http://example.co` passes against `discourseUrl = "http://example.com"`. Weaker than the server-side check it mirrors.

`[lens/completeness+architecture+intent]` `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11` — `postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')` uses the full referer URL (with path/query) as `targetOrigin`, which must be `scheme://host[:port]`; interpolated unescaped into a JS string literal; no fallback when referer is blank (`''` throws).

`[lens/intent]` `app/models/post.rb:131` — `return raw if cook_method == raw_html` bypasses `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)` and the sanitizing pipeline for exactly the least-trusted content (remote HTML), which is then rendered via `raw post.cooked` at `best.html.erb:19`.

`[lens/architecture+completeness]` `app/models/topic_embed.rb:48` and `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29` — `open()` with no timeout, no size cap, no redirect handling, no scheme/host restriction; can pin a Sidekiq worker. `poll_feed` is `retry: false`, so a transient failure silently drops the poll.

`[lens/architecture]` `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:28` — `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` is a non-standard value; it works only because browsers ignore invalid values. Lower confidence — this was the Discourse idiom at the time.

`[lens/intent]` Overall — `git grep embeddable_host HEAD~2` returns nothing: there was no prior embed system to "enhance." This is net-new feature construction; the entire validation surface is 4 checks. Substantial drift from the title.

`[lens/completeness+intent]` `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:9` — `embed_url` is never validated in the controller (only the *referer* is). `params.require` raises `ParameterMissing` → 500, not 4xx. A garbage `embed_url` is accepted, a job enqueued, `TopicRetriever` silently rejects it, and the client loops on `loading` reloading every 30s forever with no failure state.

`[lens/completeness+architecture+intent]` `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26` + `lib/topic_retriever.rb:15` — host authorization is implemented twice, independently, with no shared owner: controller checks the referer, retriever checks the embed_url, neither normalizes scheme/port/`www.`/case. Single scalar setting, no whitelist. `config/site_settings.yml:353` has no validator, so an admin entering `http://example.com` silently disables embedding with no error.

`[lens/completeness]` `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:36` — feed items are imported with **no** `embeddable_host` check, unlike `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`. Whitelist enforcement is inconsistent between the two import entry points.

`[lens/feasibility+architecture+completeness]` `app/models/topic_embed.rb:24` — `PostCreator#create` returns a `Post` with errors (not nil) on failure, so `post.present?` is true with `id == nil`; `TopicEmbed.create!(post_id: nil)` then violates the `null: false` constraint. Should check `post.persisted?`/`creator.errors.blank?`.

`[lens/completeness+architecture]` `app/models/topic_embed.rb:15` and `lib/topic_retriever.rb:37` — check-then-create TOCTOU: two concurrent jobs both see `embed.blank?` and both insert, hitting the unique index with an unrescued `RecordNotUnique`.

`[lens/completeness+architecture]` `app/models/topic_embed.rb:31` — update path has no transaction (create path does), no nil check on `embed.post`, never updates the topic title when the source title changes, and `update_column(:content_sha1, ...)` runs unconditionally even when `revise!` returns false — recording a failed revision as synced so it never retries.

`[lens/completeness+intent+architecture]` `app/models/topic_embed.rb:13` — `contents << ...` mutates the caller's string in place; re-import of the same object double-appends the "Imported from" footer. Also raises on nil/frozen content.

`[lens/completeness+intent]` `app/models/topic_embed.rb:64` — `absolutize_urls` only handles leading-`/` URLs. Protocol-relative (`//cdn.example.com/x.png`) get rewritten to `http://origin-host/cdn.example.com/x.png`; document-relative (`images/x.png`) are left untouched and resolve against the Discourse host. RSS is the explicitly stated motivating case (line 55 comment). No spec covers either.
`[lens/completeness]` `app/models/topic_embed.rb:57` — `URI(url)` can raise `URI::InvalidURIError` on URLs with unescaped chars that still pass the `/^https?:\/\//` guard at line 11.

`[lens/completeness]` `app/models/topic_embed.rb:79` — no URL normalization before lookup: `http://x/a`, `http://x/a/`, `https://x/a`, `?utm_source=…` each create a separate topic. The unique index doesn't help since the strings differ.

`[lens/feasibility+completeness]` `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35` — `i.content.scrub` assumes non-nil `content`; SimpleRSS populates `content` only from `content:encoded`, so common RSS 2.0 feeds (description-only) raise `NoMethodError`. No per-item rescue, so one bad item aborts the whole batch. `String#scrub` also requires Ruby ≥ 2.1 with no version pin in the repo.

`[lens/completeness+architecture]` `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:5` — no guard for a missing `#discourse-comments` element or undefined `discourseUrl`/`discourseEmbedUrl`; the script throws and the embed silently does nothing. Nothing in the diff generates or serves this snippet.

`[lens/completeness]` `app/views/embed/best.html.erb:11` — no guard for a `TopicEmbed` row pointing at a deleted topic/post; `topic_id_for_embed` returns the stale id and the page 500s. No `dependent: :destroy`/FK/cleanup exists.

`[lens/architecture]` `lib/topic_retriever.rb:41` — `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` runs a *scheduled* job inline from a lib object inside `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`. A single per-URL request triggers a full unbounded feed poll plus N imports, bypassing `recurrence { hourly }` and `retry: false` semantics.

`[lens/architecture]` `lib/topic_retriever.rb:26` — hand-rolled `$redis.setnx`/`expire` throttle duplicating Discourse's existing `RateLimiter` (used at `lib/post_creator.rb:3`, `lib/tasks/disqus.thor:139`); hardcoded 60s window, unnamespaced key `retrieved:<url>` not site/multisite-scoped.
`[lens/architecture]` `app/models/topic_embed.rb:44` — an ActiveRecord model performs outbound HTTP and HTML extraction; that belongs in `TopicRetriever`, which already exists for exactly this.

`[lens/architecture]` `app/models/topic_embed.rb:1` — `require_dependency 'nokogiri'` uses the Rails autoload helper for a gem; should be plain `require` (compare `require 'digest/sha1'` in poll_feed.rb).
`[lens/architecture]` `app/models/topic_embed.rb:22` — `skip_validations: true` opts arbitrary remote HTML out of all `Post` invariants rather than modeling an explicit trusted-import concept.
`[lens/architecture]` `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:13` — `{best: 5}` is a hardcoded magic constant while every other tunable in the feature became a site setting.

`[lens/architecture]` `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:19` — `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` applies uniformly to both the "topic exists" and "still loading" responses, which have very different cacheability.

`[lens/completeness+architecture]` `app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss:1` / `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:4` — `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'` from a non-application layout, but no `config.assets.precompile` registration for `embed.css`/`embed.js` anywhere in the diff → will not resolve in production.

`[lens/scope+intent]` `lib/tasks/disqus.thor:117` — `--category`/`-c` option and its `Category.where(name:)` lookup deleted outright. Anyone scripting with `-c` now gets a Thor unknown-option failure; imported topics can no longer be categorized. Not required by the embed work.

`[lens/scope+intent+architecture]` `lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148` — swapped `PostCreator.new(..., created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category:)` for `TopicEmbed.import_remote`. Silent losses: original Disqus timestamps dropped (child posts at line 164 still set `created_at`, so parent/child dates now disagree), and an offline XML import became network-dependent — `import_remote` returns nil for dead links and the `if post.present?` guard then drops that thread's entire reply set silently.
`[lens/scope]` `db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb:3,33` — pure whitespace noise plus trailing-newline removal in an unrelated historical migration.

`[lens/scope]` `lib/post_revisor.rb:14` — formatting-only hunk (blank line removed) bundled with the functional change. The functional part at line 85 is genuinely required and opt-in, so no behavior change for existing callers.

`[lens/completeness+intent+architecture]` `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20` — `feed_key` is defined but never called anywhere. The Last-Modified/ETag conditional-fetch it implies was never implemented; every hourly poll refetches and re-hashes the whole feed.
`[lens/feasibility+intent+architecture]` `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:1` — `require_dependency 'email/sender'` unused; copy-paste leftover.

`[lens/completeness+intent]` `config/locales/server.en.yml:37` — `embed.permalink` defined but never referenced (confirmed by grep). Conversely, the two `Discourse::InvalidAccess` messages at `embed_controller.rb:25-30` are hardcoded English with no i18n key.

`[lens/completeness]` `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:12` — only the three `execute` guard conditions are tested; `poll_feed` itself (user lookup, parse, link-vs-id fallback, unescaping, import) has zero coverage. `import_remote` likewise has zero coverage despite being the path used by both `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` and the Disqus importer.

This checkout is **sparse** — `git ls-files` returns only the 29 files in the diff, and the new files were pre-created empty at the base commit. There is no `ApplicationController`, `TopicView`, `Enum`, `Jobs::Base`, or `db/schema.rb`. Cross-file references outside the diff could not be verified, and the feasibility lens correctly excluded them rather than reporting them as fabricated paths. **No fabricated paths were found within the verifiable surface.**

Confirmed clean: all `embed.*` i18n keys used in views/model exist; `admin.site_settings.categories.embedding` matches the new `embedding:` category; the shorthand `key: ''` site-setting form matches existing usage in that file; the `get 'embed/best'` route maps correctly; `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic)` matches `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`; both new gems are actually used and the lockfile edit is internally consistent (transitive deps present, correct alphabetical position, `DEPENDENCIES` updated); `content_sha1 limit: 40` matches `Digest::SHA1.hexdigest`; `bypass_rate_limiter` is a real `PostRevisor` opt; all changed `.rb` files parse cleanly.

The single highest-value fix is `best.html.erb:6` — one character (`end if` → `end`) stands between this feature and never rendering at all, and it survives CI only because no spec calls `render_views`.

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

However, `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` sets `TopicRetriever.expects(:new).returns(retriever)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)` in the "no previous embed" example. `[lens/feasibility+architecture]` `app/models/topic_embed.rb:48` — `open(url).read` with no `require 'open-uri'` in the file. Only `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:7` requires it; `import_remote` is reached from `lib/topic_retriever.rb:52` and `lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148` on paths that never load poll_feed, where `Kernel#open` treats the URL as a filename → `Errno::ENOENT`.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `app/models/topic_embed.rb#import_remote` the code calls `open(url).read` but the file does not `require 'open-uri'`. Without `open-uri`, Ruby’s `Kernel#open` treats the string as a local filename (e.g. "http://...") and will raise `Errno::ENOENT` rather than fetching HTTP. The only added `require 'open-uri'` in this diff is in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, but `import_remote` is invoked from `lib/topic_retriever.rb#fetch_http` and `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` paths that do not load `poll_feed.rb`, so there is no guarantee `open-uri` is loaded before `open(url)` is executed.

Editing shipped migrations is unsafe; `force: true` issues `DROP TABLE` on any environment not yet past this version. Nothing in the embed feature touches `top_topics`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff modifies an existing migration `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`, changing `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists before recreating it, which can cause data loss in environments where this migration is run (or re-run) and the table already exists. This change is unrelated to the embedding feature shown elsewhere in the diff and introduces a real risk by altering a previously committed migration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `[lens/feasibility+architecture+completeness]` `db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3` — `force: true` on a new table silently drops/recreates rather than failing loudly; not the convention elsewhere in the repo.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` does use `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`, which would drop/recreate the table if it already existed. However, this is a new table migration that normally runs once on a DB where `topic_embeds` does not exist, so it doesn’t introduce a concrete bug/correctness issue in normal operation—at most it’s a convention/style/risk preference. Also, the diff itself changes another migration (`create_top_topics`) to add `force: true`, so it’s not clearly “not the convention elsewhere” within the changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `[lens/completeness+architecture]` `db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:4` — no indexes on `topic_id`/`post_id` despite both being queried/joined; no FKs; `embed_url` is a plain 255-char `:string` under a unique index, truncating longer canonical URLs.

`[lens/architecture]` `db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3` — `default: 1` hardcodes the numeric value of `Post.cook_methods[:regular]`; reordering the enum in `app/models/post.rb:63` silently desyncs the column default.

adjudication.rationale: The migration adds `cook_method` with `default: 1`, while `Post.cook_methods` is defined as an ordered enum `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`. It is true that this couples the DB default to the enum’s numeric mapping, but the claimed “silent desync” only happens if someone later reorders the enum—there’s no evidence in the diff that such a reorder occurs or that `1` is currently wrong. Given existing Discourse patterns (e.g., `post_type` enums historically default to `1` for `:regular`), this is not a verifiable bug introduced by the diff, but a speculative future-maintenance concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `[lens/intent+architecture]` `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:19` — `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring test, not origin equality. `http://example.co` passes against `discourseUrl = "http://example.com"`. Weaker than the server-side check it mirrors.
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify the same core vulnerability: using `indexOf` for origin validation performs a substring check rather than strict origin equality, allowing malicious lookalike domains (e.g., `evil-discourseUrl.com` or `example.co` vs `example.com`) to bypass the check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `[lens/completeness+architecture+intent]` `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11` — `postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')` uses the full referer URL (with path/query) as `targetOrigin`, which must be `scheme://host[:port]`; interpolated unescaped into a JS string literal; no fallback when referer is blank (`''` throws).
matched_golden_ids: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that `postMessage` is using the full referrer URL (including path/query) as `targetOrigin` and explains that `targetOrigin` must be just the origin (scheme+host+port), which aligns with the golden issue about messages being dropped due to incorrect targetOrigin. Extra notes (escaping, blank referer) don’t change the core match.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `[lens/intent]` `app/models/post.rb:131` — `return raw if cook_method == raw_html` bypasses `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)` and the sanitizing pipeline for exactly the least-trusted content (remote HTML), which is then rendered via `raw post.cooked` at `best.html.erb:19`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces a new `cook_method` enum with `:raw_html` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which skips the normal cooking/sanitization path (`post_analyzer.cook` + `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`). The new feed/import code sets `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` when creating posts from remote content (`TopicEmbed.import` called by `Jobs::PollFeed` and `TopicEmbed.import_remote`), and the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`. Since the imported content originates from external sources (RSS `i.content` / Readability output) and is not passed through the standard sanitizing pipeline, this is a verifiable XSS/unsafe HTML rendering issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `[lens/architecture+completeness]` `app/models/topic_embed.rb:48` and `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29` — `open()` with no timeout, no size cap, no redirect handling, no scheme/host restriction; can pin a Sidekiq worker. `poll_feed` is `retry: false`, so a transient failure silently drops the poll.
matched_golden_ids: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Golden issue is SSRF risk: PollFeed calls open() on a configurable URL (feed_polling_url) without validation, letting an attacker force arbitrary URL fetches. The candidate flags open() usage in poll_feed with no scheme/host restriction, which is the same core vulnerability (unrestricted URL fetching), even though it also discusses timeouts/worker pinning and retries.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `[lens/architecture]` `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:28` — `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` is a non-standard value; it works only because browsers ignore invalid values. Lower confidence — this was the Discourse idiom at the time.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, the diff explicitly sets `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL"`. The standard/recognized X-Frame-Options directives are `DENY`, `SAMEORIGIN`, and the obsolete `ALLOW-FROM`; `ALLOWALL` is not a valid directive. That makes the header behavior browser-dependent (some browsers may ignore the header entirely when invalid), so it’s a real, verifiable correctness/security-control issue introduced by the diff (it may fail to reliably permit framing, or fail open/closed depending on user agent/defaults).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `[lens/intent]` Overall — `git grep embeddable_host HEAD~2` returns nothing: there was no prior embed system to "enhance." This is net-new feature construction; the entire validation surface is 4 checks. Substantial drift from the title.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is about commit/PR intent (“enhance” vs net-new) and claims based on `git grep ... HEAD~2`, which is not verifiable from the provided diff alone and is not itself a bug/security/correctness defect in the code. The statement that the “validation surface is 4 checks” is descriptive but does not identify a concrete defect introduced by the diff. No specific, verifiable functional problem is pointed out in the changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `[lens/completeness+intent]` `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:9` — `embed_url` is never validated in the controller (only the *referer* is). `params.require` raises `ParameterMissing` → 500, not 4xx. A garbage `embed_url` is accepted, a job enqueued, `TopicRetriever` silently rejects it, and the client loops on `loading` reloading every 30s forever with no failure state.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, the only gate is `params.require(:embed_url)` plus `ensure_embeddable` which validates the *referer* host, not the `embed_url` param. As a result, a request with a valid referer (matching `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`) but a garbage `embed_url` (e.g. `"not a url"` or a different host) will pass `ensure_embeddable`, find no existing `TopicEmbed`, enqueue `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`, and render `loading`. The job then calls `TopicRetriever`, which will reject invalid/different-host URLs (`URI(@embed_url)` rescue / host mismatch) and do nothing, so the embed will never be created. The `loading.html.erb` page always reloads every 30s with no failure state, so this can loop indefinitely. (The sub-claim that `ParameterMissing` necessarily becomes a 500 is not guaranteed—Rails commonly maps it to 400—but the “garbage embed_url leads to endless loading” behavior is directly supported by the diff.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: `[lens/completeness+architecture+intent]` `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26` + `lib/topic_retriever.rb:15` — host authorization is implemented twice, independently, with no shared owner: controller checks the referer, retriever checks the embed_url, neither normalizes scheme/port/`www.`/case. Single scalar setting, no whitelist. `config/site_settings.yml:353` has no validator, so an admin entering `http://example.com` silently disables embedding with no error.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff shows two separate host-authorization checks implemented in different places with different inputs: `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` compares `URI(request.referer).host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, while `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` compares `URI(@embed_url).host` to the same setting. Neither normalizes the configured value (e.g., stripping scheme/port, downcasing, handling `www.`), and the setting is defined as a free string (`embeddable_host: ''` in `config/site_settings.yml`) with no validator in this diff. As a result, if an admin enters `http://example.com` (or includes a port, uppercase, trailing slash, etc.), both checks will fail (`URI(...).host` is `example.com`), effectively disabling embedding without a clear error message beyond “invalid referer host” / the retriever refusing to run. The duplication itself is verifiable in the diff and can lead to inconsistent/fragile behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `[lens/completeness]` `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:36` — feed items are imported with **no** `embeddable_host` check, unlike `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`. Whitelist enforcement is inconsistent between the two import entry points.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds two import paths: (1) on-demand via `TopicRetriever`, which blocks retrieval unless `URI(@embed_url).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (`invalid_host?`), and (2) scheduled `Jobs::PollFeed`, which fetches `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url` and imports each item via `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)` without any host/whitelist check. `TopicEmbed.import` only checks the URL scheme (`/^https?\:\/\//`) and does not enforce `embeddable_host`. Therefore feed-based importing can create/update topics for URLs on any host (whatever the feed contains), which is inconsistent with the whitelist enforcement in `TopicRetriever` and is a verifiable gap in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `[lens/feasibility+architecture+completeness]` `app/models/topic_embed.rb:24` — `PostCreator#create` returns a `Post` with errors (not nil) on failure, so `post.present?` is true with `id == nil`; `TopicEmbed.create!(post_id: nil)` then violates the `null: false` constraint. Should check `post.persisted?`/`creator.errors.blank?`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `TopicEmbed.import` calling `creator = PostCreator.new(...)` then `post = creator.create` and guarding with `if post.present?` before `TopicEmbed.create!`. However, the claim that `PostCreator#create` returns a non-persisted `Post` object (with `id == nil`) on failure is not demonstrated anywhere in the diff (the implementation of `PostCreator#create` is not shown/changed). Existing code in the diff/base (e.g., the prior Disqus import) also used `post.present?` as the success check, suggesting the project convention is that `create` returns `nil` on failure. Therefore the finding depends on unverified behavior outside the diff and is not a strictly verifiable defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `[lens/completeness+architecture]` `app/models/topic_embed.rb:15` and `lib/topic_retriever.rb:37` — check-then-create TOCTOU: two concurrent jobs both see `embed.blank?` and both insert, hitting the unique index with an unrescued `RecordNotUnique`.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, later does `TopicEmbed.create!(..., embed_url: url, ...)` inside a transaction. With the new unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`, two concurrent importers can both observe no row and then both attempt `create!`, causing one to raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` (or equivalent) and it is not rescued in this method. `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` adds an additional check-then-act (`exists?` then later import) that can also race, so concurrency can still hit the same unhandled uniqueness violation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `[lens/completeness+architecture]` `app/models/topic_embed.rb:31` — update path has no transaction (create path does), no nil check on `embed.post`, never updates the topic title when the source title changes, and `update_column(:content_sha1, ...)` runs unconditionally even when `revise!` returns false — recording a failed revision as synced so it never retries.

adjudication.rationale:
In `TopicEmbed.import`’s update branch, it does `post = embed.post` and then, if the SHA differs, calls `revisor.revise!(...)` and *always* follows with `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)`.

This is verifiable in the diff and is a correctness risk because `PostRevisor#revise!` can return `false` (it explicitly `return false if not should_revise?`), so the code can record the embed as “synced” even when the post was not actually revised—preventing future retries since `content_sha1` will now match.

Also, the update path has no transaction while the create path wraps changes in `Topic.transaction`, so a failure between revising the post and updating `content_sha1` (or vice versa) can leave the system in an inconsistent state. The “never updates the topic title” point is more of a feature/behavior choice and not clearly a defect from the diff alone, but the unconditional `update_column` after a potentially-failed `revise!` is a real bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `[lens/completeness+intent+architecture]` `app/models/topic_embed.rb:13` — `contents << ...` mutates the caller's string in place; re-import of the same object double-appends the "Imported from" footer. Also raises on nil/frozen content.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the line `contents << "\n<hr>..."` mutates the `contents` argument in place. That is a verifiable side effect: any caller holding the same String instance will see it modified (and repeated calls with the same object would append the footer multiple times). Additionally, if `contents` is `nil` or a frozen string, this line will raise (`NoMethodError`/`FrozenError`) because there is no presence/dup/freeze handling in the method.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `[lens/completeness+intent]` `app/models/topic_embed.rb:64` — `absolutize_urls` only handles leading-`/` URLs. Protocol-relative (`//cdn.example.com/x.png`) get rewritten to `http://origin-host/cdn.example.com/x.png`; document-relative (`images/x.png`) are left untouched and resolve against the Discourse host. RSS is the explicitly stated motivating case (line 55 comment). No spec covers either.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, links/images are only rewritten when `href/src.start_with?('/')`. That condition also matches protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/x.png`, which will be transformed into `"#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}"` => `http://origin-host/cdn.example.com/x.png`, an incorrect URL. Additionally, document-relative paths like `images/x.png` do not start with `/` and are left unchanged, so when rendered inside Discourse they will resolve relative to the Discourse host/path rather than the source site. The existing spec only covers root-relative (`/hello`, `/images/...`) and does not cover either `//...` or `images/...` cases. This is a concrete correctness issue in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `[lens/completeness]` `app/models/topic_embed.rb:57` — `URI(url)` can raise `URI::InvalidURIError` on URLs with unescaped chars that still pass the `/^https?:\/\//` guard at line 11.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicEmbed.import` only checks `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` and then calls `absolutize_urls(url, contents)`, which does `uri = URI(url)` without rescue. `URI()`/`URI.parse` can raise `URI::InvalidURIError` for URLs containing unescaped characters (e.g., spaces, `{}`, `|`, etc.) even though they still start with `http://` or `https://` and pass the regex guard. This would cause the import (RSS polling / remote import) to crash for such feed items.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `[lens/completeness]` `app/models/topic_embed.rb:79` — no URL normalization before lookup: `http://x/a`, `http://x/a/`, `https://x/a`, `?utm_source=…` each create a separate topic. The unique index doesn't help since the strings differ.

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: TopicEmbed uses the raw URL string as the primary identity key everywhere (TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first in .import, TopicEmbed.create!/add_index unique on :embed_url, and .topic_id_for_embed(embed_url) does an exact-match query). There is no canonicalization/normalization step (scheme, trailing slash, query params like utm_*, fragment, etc.). As a result, semantically identical pages such as http://x/a vs http://x/a/ vs https://x/a or URLs with tracking params will be treated as distinct and can create duplicate topics; the unique index won’t prevent this because the stored strings differ.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `[lens/feasibility+completeness]` `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35` — `i.content.scrub` assumes non-nil `content`; SimpleRSS populates `content` only from `content:encoded`, so common RSS 2.0 feeds (description-only) raise `NoMethodError`. No per-item rescue, so one bad item aborts the whole batch. `String#scrub` also requires Ruby ≥ 2.1 with no version pin in the repo.
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Candidate flags the same core bug: calling `i.content.scrub` assumes `i.content` exists, but many RSS feeds provide only `description` (no `content`/`content:encoded`), causing `NoMethodError`/nil dereference. It also adds extra related notes (batch abort, Ruby version), but the underlying issue matches the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `[lens/completeness+architecture]` `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:5` — no guard for a missing `#discourse-comments` element or undefined `discourseUrl`/`discourseEmbedUrl`; the script throws and the embed silently does nothing. Nothing in the diff generates or serves this snippet.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the code immediately reads `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and then unconditionally does `comments.appendChild(iframe)`. If the host page doesn’t include an element with id `discourse-comments`, `comments` is `null` and this will throw at runtime. It also concatenates `discourseUrl` and `discourseEmbedUrl` into `iframe.src` without any `typeof` checks; if either global is undefined, it will throw a `ReferenceError` before doing anything. These failure modes are directly verifiable from the diff. (The claim about “nothing in the diff generates or serves this snippet” is less provable since assets can be served via the asset pipeline without being referenced in a view, but the missing guards/runtime exceptions are real.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: `[lens/completeness]` `app/views/embed/best.html.erb:11` — no guard for a `TopicEmbed` row pointing at a deleted topic/post; `topic_id_for_embed` returns the stale id and the page 500s. No `dependent: :destroy`/FK/cleanup exists.

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` simply plucks `topic_id` from `topic_embeds` (`TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: embed_url).pluck(:topic_id).first`) without verifying the referenced `topics`/`posts` still exist. The migration `create_topic_embeds` adds no foreign keys, and the `TopicEmbed` model adds no cleanup mechanism; nothing in the diff adds `dependent: :destroy` on the owning `Topic`/`Post` side either. In `EmbedController#best`, a non-nil `topic_id` leads directly to `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)`, and the view assumes `@topic_view.topic` is present (`@topic_view.topic.url`). If a topic/post is deleted while the `topic_embeds` row remains, this path can raise (e.g., RecordNotFound / nil topic) and result in an unhandled error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `[lens/architecture]` `lib/topic_retriever.rb:41` — `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` runs a *scheduled* job inline from a lib object inside `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`. A single per-URL request triggers a full unbounded feed poll plus N imports, bypassing `recurrence { hourly }` and `retry: false` semantics.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it directly invokes `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline (lib object called from `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`, which is enqueued per missing-embed request). This bypasses the scheduled job’s `recurrence { hourly }` (and any scheduler-controlled semantics like when it runs) and will fetch/parse the entire feed (`SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` then `rss.items.each`) on-demand. That means a single embed retrieval can trigger a full feed poll + N `TopicEmbed.import` operations, and repeated requests for different `embed_url`s can cause repeated full polls, which is an architectural/performance/correctness concern verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `[lens/architecture]` `lib/topic_retriever.rb:26` — hand-rolled `$redis.setnx`/`expire` throttle duplicating Discourse's existing `RateLimiter` (used at `lib/post_creator.rb:3`, `lib/tasks/disqus.thor:139`); hardcoded 60s window, unnamespaced key `retrieved:<url>` not site/multisite-scoped.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a custom throttle in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` using `$redis.setnx` + `expire` with a hardcoded 60s and a key of `"retrieved:#{@embed_url}"`. However, the finding’s core claim that this *duplicates Discourse’s existing `RateLimiter`* and points to its use at specific locations is not verifiable from this diff (those referenced lines/usages aren’t shown here), and whether `$redis` is already namespaced per-site/multisite is also not established by the diff alone. So while the pattern could be debated architecturally, the proposed finding relies on assumptions outside the provided changes rather than a clear, self-evident defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `[lens/architecture]` `app/models/topic_embed.rb:44` — an ActiveRecord model performs outbound HTTP and HTML extraction; that belongs in `TopicRetriever`, which already exists for exactly this.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (in `app/models/topic_embed.rb`) doing outbound HTTP (`open(url).read`) and HTML extraction (`Readability::Document.new(...)`). However, the proposed finding is an architectural preference (separation of concerns) rather than a clear defect/bug/security/correctness problem introduced by the diff. `TopicRetriever` already calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, so this placement doesn’t break behavior; it’s not verifiably wrong from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `[lens/architecture]` `app/models/topic_embed.rb:1` — `require_dependency 'nokogiri'` uses the Rails autoload helper for a gem; should be plain `require` (compare `require 'digest/sha1'` in poll_feed.rb).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `require_dependency 'nokogiri'` at the top of `app/models/topic_embed.rb`. While `require_dependency` is typically used for reloadable app code (and `require` is more common for gems), `require_dependency` will still load the gem via Ruby's `require` mechanism and does not introduce a clear bug, security issue, or correctness defect in this change. The finding is essentially an architectural/style preference/inconsistency, not a verifiable problem.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `[lens/architecture]` `app/models/topic_embed.rb:22` — `skip_validations: true` opts arbitrary remote HTML out of all `Post` invariants rather than modeling an explicit trusted-import concept.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, when creating a new post it calls `PostCreator.new(..., raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents), skip_validations: true, cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])`. This explicitly bypasses model validations for content coming from an external URL/feed, and it is not gated behind any explicit “trusted import” concept—it's the default path for embedded imports. Given that `Post#cook` now returns `raw` unchanged for `:raw_html`, this also means imported content skips the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline, making the lack of validations/invariants a concrete security/correctness concern introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `[lens/architecture]` `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:13` — `{best: 5}` is a hardcoded magic constant while every other tunable in the feature became a site setting.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does hardcode `{best: 5}` in `EmbedController#best` when constructing `TopicView`, but this is a design/malleability preference rather than a clear defect (no correctness, security, or functional bug is demonstrated). The diff does not establish that the number of embedded “best” posts is intended to be user-configurable, nor that omitting a site setting breaks expected behavior. It’s simply a fixed default value.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `[lens/architecture]` `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:19` — `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` applies uniformly to both the "topic exists" and "still loading" responses, which have very different cacheability.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is executed unconditionally after either (a) building `@topic_view` and rendering the “best” embed or (b) rendering the `loading` template when `topic_id` is missing. This means the “loading” response will also be cacheable for 60s. Given `loading.html.erb` uses `document.location.reload()` after 30s, a cacheable response can cause the browser/proxy to serve the cached loading page again (until max-age expires) even after the background job has created the topic, delaying the transition to the real content. The two responses do have different cacheability needs, so applying the same expires header to both is a concrete correctness/behavior issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `[lens/completeness+architecture]` `app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss:1` / `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:4` — `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'` from a non-application layout, but no `config.assets.precompile` registration for `embed.css`/`embed.js` anywhere in the diff → will not resolve in production.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new standalone stylesheet `app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss` and a new layout `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb` that references it via `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'`. Under the default Rails asset pipeline behavior, only `application.css`/`application.js` (and non-CSS/JS assets) are precompiled; additional top-level CSS/JS entrypoints like `embed.css`/`embed.js` must be either required by the main manifests or explicitly added to `config.assets.precompile`. This diff does neither (no manifest require and no precompile registration shown), so in a typical production setup (`config.assets.compile = false`) the `embed` stylesheet would not be available.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `[lens/scope+intent+architecture]` `lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148` — swapped `PostCreator.new(..., created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category:)` for `TopicEmbed.import_remote`. Silent losses: original Disqus timestamps dropped (child posts at line 164 still set `created_at`, so parent/child dates now disagree), and an offline XML import became network-dependent — `import_remote` returns nil for dead links and the `if post.present?` guard then drops that thread's entire reply set silently.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the thread/topic “root” post creation was changed from `PostCreator.new(..., created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), ...)` to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` ultimately calls `PostCreator.new` without passing any `created_at`, so the imported topic’s timestamp will default to “now” rather than the Disqus thread’s original timestamp—this is a concrete regression visible in the diff. Also, `import_remote` performs `open(url).read` on `t[:link]`, making the import depend on network access/live URLs rather than just the XML payload; that dependency change is explicit in the diff. The “silent drop” aspect is directionally plausible because the code still gates reply import on `if post.present?`, but a dead link is more likely to raise from `open` than return nil (so it may fail loudly rather than silently).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The single highest-value fix is `best.html.erb:6` — one character (`end if` → `end`) stands between this feature and never rendering at all, and it survives CI only because no spec calls `render_views`.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` the header block is closed with `<%- end if %>`. In Ruby/ERB, `end` closes the `if` block; appending `if` (without a condition) makes the embedded Ruby code syntactically invalid (`end if` is not valid Ruby here). Rendering this template would raise a template syntax error, so the embed page would fail to render; the existing controller specs don’t render views, so they wouldn’t catch it.
